newsitem.title: USA: MedCare says opens first clinic.
newsitem.headline: MedCare says opens first clinic.

text.p: MedCare Technologies Inc said it opened in Norman, Okla., the first in a planned nationwide network of clinics for the treatment of urinary incontinence.
MedCare said its new treatment protocol does not require U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval and is covered by most health insurance plans.
The protocol typically requires six to eight visits over three to four months, the company said.

The program includes electromyographic biofeedback, pelvic floor muscle exercises and bladder and bowel retraining. It is designed to activate and strengthen various sensory-response mechanisms that maintain bladder and bowel control, it said.

"The non-invasive, non-surgical and drug-free treatment has a proven success rate in excess of 87 percent," MedCare said, adding it plans to open additional clinics in Overland Park, Kan., Florida, Arizona, New York and Los Angeles.
